name: Web & Browser Security
description: Attacks and defenses for the web platform: browsers, JavaScript, the DOM, web apps, and server-side web code.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this list shows web security splitting along two tracks. One track targets the server-side web application itself: "NAVEX: Precise and Scalable Exploit Generation for Dynamic Web Applications" (2018) automatically builds exploits for dynamic web apps, while "Freezing the Web: A Study of ReDoS Vulnerabilities in JavaScript-based Web Servers" (2018) and "Rampart: Protecting Web Applications from CPU-Exhaustion Denial-of-Service Attacks" (2018) tackle algorithmic and resource-exhaustion denial of service in JavaScript backends. The other track is microarchitectural: "Foreshadow: Extracting the Keys to the Intel SGX Kingdom with Transient Out-of-Order Execution" (2018) showed that the hardware underneath the browser and the web stack could leak secrets, foreshadowing a long line of transient-execution and side-channel work relevant to the web platform.

By 2019 the focus broadened to the JavaScript supply chain and the browser's own architecture. "Small World with High Risks: A Study of Security Threats in the npm Ecosystem" (2019) quantified how deeply transitive npm dependencies expose web developers, and "Less is More: Quantifying the Security Benefits of Debloating Web Applications" (2019) pushed attack-surface reduction as a defense. On the browser side, "Site Isolation: Process Separation for Web Sites within the Browser" (2019) documented Chrome's move to put each site in its own process, a structural defense against cross-site leaks. In-process isolation primitives like "ERIM: Secure, Efficient In-process Isolation with Protection Keys (MPK)" (2019) and later "Donky: Domain Keys - Efficient In-Process Isolation for RISC-V and x86" (2020) gave finer-grained ways to wall off sensitive state inside a single process.

Around 2020 two themes matured. First, the web platform's runtime targets grew more sophisticated: "Everything Old is New Again: Binary Security of WebAssembly" (2020) showed that Wasm reintroduced classic memory-safety hazards in the browser, and "Montage: A Neural Network Language Model-Guided JavaScript Engine Fuzzer" (2020) brought learning-based fuzzing to JS engines that ship to billions of browsers. Second, phishing became a measurement-and-detection powerhouse, with "Sunrise to Sunset: Analyzing the End-to-end Life Cycle and Effectiveness of Phishing Attacks at Scale" (2020) and "PhishTime: Continuous Longitudinal Measurement of the Effectiveness of Anti-phishing Blacklists" (2020) probing the defense ecosystem at scale.

The most recent work shows two clear endpoints. Hardware attacks reached back up into the browser sandbox itself: "SMASH: Synchronized Many-sided Rowhammer Attacks from JavaScript" (2021) triggered Rowhammer bit flips straight from web JavaScript, collapsing the gap between microarchitecture and the web platform. Meanwhile phishing defense turned visual and deep-learning-driven, from "Phishpedia: A Hybrid Deep Learning Based Approach to Visually Identify Phishing Webpages" (2021) to "Inferring Phishing Intention via Webpage Appearance and Dynamics: A Deep Vision Based Approach" (2022), reflecting where the field stands now: defending real users of the web through perception-based detection while still patching deep platform and hardware weaknesses.

milestones.title: NAVEX: Precise and Scalable Exploit Generation for Dynamic Web Applications
milestones.note: scaled automated exploit generation to real dynamic web applications, advancing server-side web app analysis

milestones.title: Small World with High Risks: A Study of Security Threats in the npm Ecosystem
milestones.note: exposed the systemic risk of transitive JavaScript dependencies, framing the web supply chain as a security problem

milestones.title: Site Isolation: Process Separation for Web Sites within the Browser
milestones.note: documented Chrome's per-site process architecture, a foundational structural browser defense against cross-site leaks

milestones.title: Everything Old is New Again: Binary Security of WebAssembly
milestones.note: revealed that WebAssembly reintroduces classic memory-safety hazards into the browser

milestones.title: Montage: A Neural Network Language Model-Guided JavaScript Engine Fuzzer
milestones.note: brought language-model-guided fuzzing to JS engines, targeting a core component of every browser

milestones.title: Phishpedia: A Hybrid Deep Learning Based Approach to Visually Identify Phishing Webpages
milestones.note: shifted phishing defense toward visual deep-learning identification of malicious webpages
